proposals.before: In the fourth month of the third year (997), Jiao Wo, vice horse-and-arms commander of the Shenqi Army, presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; ordered to demonstrate them, he wheeled about on horseback as if flying, and was promoted to command that army.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of the third year (1000), Jiao Wo, vice horse-and-arms commander of the Shenqi Army, presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; ordered to demonstrate them, he wheeled about on horseback as if flying, and was promoted to command that army.
proposals.reason: Xianping 3 corresponds to AD 1000, not 997; the parenthetical Western year is wrong.

proposals.before: In the fifth year (999), Liu Yongxi, commissioner of Ninghua Army, devised a hand cannon and presented it; the court ordered the border commands to build them for service.
proposals.after: In the fifth year (1002), Liu Yongxi, commissioner of Ninghua Army, devised a hand cannon and presented it; the court ordered the border commands to build them for service.
proposals.reason: Xianping 5 corresponds to AD 1002, not 999.

proposals.before: In the tenth month of the sixth year (1001), message tokens were issued to the army.
proposals.after: In the tenth month of the sixth year (1003), message tokens were issued to the army.
proposals.reason: Xianping 6 corresponds to AD 1003, not 1001.

proposals.before: Wang An submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuandi of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
proposals.after: Wang Pang submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuandi of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
proposals.reason: 王雱 is Wang Pang (Wang Anshi's son), not Wang An; the idiomatic name collapses him with 安石.

proposals.before: In sum, An's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
proposals.after: In sum, Pang's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
proposals.reason: 雱 refers to Wang Pang; 'An' wrongly suggests Wang Anshi.

proposals.before: Wang An argued that since antiquity the south had repeatedly beaten Chinese armies with elephants and that Shilong's plan deserved trial; he also expounded classical chariot doctrine and proposed a chariot-versus-cavalry test.
proposals.after: Wang Anshi argued that since antiquity the south had repeatedly beaten Chinese armies with elephants and that Shilong's plan deserved trial; he also expounded classical chariot doctrine and proposed a chariot-versus-cavalry test.
proposals.reason: 安石 is Wang Anshi; idiomatic 'Wang An' confuses him with 王雱 rendered the same way.

proposals.before: Wang An said: "That is exactly right.
proposals.after: Wang Anshi said: "That is exactly right.
proposals.reason: 安石 is Wang Anshi, not Wang An.

proposals.before: Wang An added: "The court seeks only fairness in governance."
proposals.after: Wang Anshi added: "The court seeks only fairness in governance."
proposals.reason: 安石 is Wang Anshi, not Wang An.

proposals.before: In the end Wang An's rhetoric dispelled the emperor's doubts, and the directorate escaped charges of fraud.
proposals.after: In the end Wang Anshi's rhetoric dispelled the emperor's doubts, and the directorate escaped charges of fraud.
proposals.reason: 安石 is Wang Anshi, not Wang An.

proposals.before: In the eighth month, at Zhao Zhi's request, Huanqing received one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.
proposals.after: In the eighth month, at Zhao Xie's request, Huanqing received one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.
proposals.reason: 趙禼 is Zhao Xie; Zhi is an incorrect romanization of 禼.

proposals.before: In Chongning 3 the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions reported: "If Xu Yankui's chariot pattern is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.
proposals.after: In Chongning 3 the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions reported: "If Xu Yangui's chariot pattern is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.
proposals.reason: 許彥圭 is Xu Yangui (圭 gui), not Yankui.

proposals.before: The court nonetheless adopted Xu Yankui's design.
proposals.after: The court nonetheless adopted Xu Yangui's design.
proposals.reason: 許彥圭 is Xu Yangui, not Yankui.

proposals.before: These chariots reached the court through Yao Lin promoting Xu Yankui's design.
proposals.after: These chariots reached the court through Yao Lin promoting Xu Yangui's design.
proposals.reason: 許彥圭 is Xu Yangui, not Yankui.

proposals.before: Yankui sought only personal promotion at the state's expense; failure to punish him would invite repetition.
proposals.after: Yangui sought only personal promotion at the state's expense; failure to punish him would invite repetition.
proposals.reason: 彥圭 should be romanized Yangui, not Yankui.

proposals.before: Yankui was eventually punished.
proposals.after: Yangui was eventually punished.
proposals.reason: 彥圭 should be romanized Yangui, not Yankui.

proposals.before: In the Jianyan era eunuch supervisor was briefly appointed then removed.
proposals.after: In the Jianyan era the eunuch Dong Que was briefly appointed supervisor then removed.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the named eunuch 董愨 present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The court trusted Lin's frontier expertise, not realizing Yankui was reckless and Lin acted from private loyalty.
proposals.after: The court trusted Lin's frontier expertise, not realizing Yangui was reckless and Lin acted from private loyalty.
proposals.reason: 彥圭 should be romanized Yangui, not Yankui.

proposals.before: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian reported: "The Jiangdu army is Han Shizhong's old command.
proposals.after: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian reported: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮江 is Zhenjiang; Jiangdu (江都) is a different place and is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian said: "The Jiangdu army is Han Shizhong's old command.
proposals.after: Huaidong chief steward Zhu Qian said: "The Zhenjiang army is Han Shizhong's old command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮江 is Zhenjiang; Jiangdu misreads the toponym.

proposals.before: He counted 8,842 crossbowmen needing 17,684 bows but found only 6,574 serviceable and asked Jiangdu headquarters to fill the gap."
proposals.after: He counted 8,842 crossbowmen needing 17,684 bows but found only 6,574 serviceable and asked Zhenjiang headquarters to fill the gap."
proposals.reason: Chinese 鎮江都統司 is the Zhenjiang command headquarters, not Jiangdu.

proposals.before: Now examining the various armies' present crossbowmen eight thousand eight hundred forty-two men, each man should use two bows—one bow for daily drill, one bow prepared for battle—altogether should use seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-four bows; only six thousand five hundred seventy-four remain, the rest all unfit for drill instruction; we beg the Jiangdu command headquarters fill the quota."
proposals.after: Now examining the various armies' present crossbowmen eight thousand eight hundred forty-two men, each man should use two bows—one bow for daily drill, one bow prepared for battle—altogether should use seventeen thousand six hundred eighty-four bows; only six thousand five hundred seventy-four remain, the rest all unfit for drill instruction; we beg the Zhenjiang command headquarters fill the quota."

proposals.before: Before long Commandery-Manufacture Wu Ting memorialized: "The divine-power bow with pellet-head arrows—in the armies' use it is truly convenient and swift; the divine-arm cannot match it."
proposals.after: Before long Overall Commander Wu Ting memorialized: "The divine-power bow with pellet-head arrows—in the armies' use it is truly convenient and swift; the divine-arm cannot match it."
proposals.reason: 都統製/都統制 is the military overall-commander title, not 'Commandery-Manufacture'.

proposals.before: Lamellae outside specified weights were discarded as waste.
proposals.after: If lamellae were required one by one to match the originally allotted weights, whenever heavy and light differed they were discarded unused, wasting labor and materials.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits the conditional that strict per-lamella weight matching itself caused wasteful discards; the literal sense matches the Chinese.

proposals.before: They also made fire-lance guns, using the world's bamboo as tubes, installing pellet nests inside; when fired like a torch, after the flame died the pellet nest shot out like cannon sound, heard more than one hundred fifty paces distant.
proposals.after: They also made fire-lance guns, using bamboo as tubes, installing pellet nests inside; when fired like a torch, after the flame died the pellet nest shot out like cannon sound, heard more than one hundred fifty paces distant.
proposals.reason: Literal 'the world's bamboo' for 世竹 is unnatural and obscures the material; idiomatic already treats it as bamboo tubing.

decisions.reason: Immediate prior unit establishes 咸平元年, so unmarked 三年四月 is Xianping 3 (AD 1000); the parenthetical 997 wrongly treats the year as Zhidao 3.
Under the continuing Xianping sequence after 咸平元年, 五年 is Xianping 5 (AD 1002), not 999.
六年十月 continues the same Xianping count, so the year is AD 1003, not 1001.
